songs.name: I'm A Hog For You Baby

ai_show_review.summary: Fiery early‑66 set with thunderous Pigpen organ and high‑energy R&B
ai_show_review.blurb: Features thunderous Pigpen organ on “I’m A Hog For You Baby”, “Hey Little One” and “You Don't Have To Ask”. Jerry’s fiery guitar and vocals drive the high‑energy R&B set, while the rhythm section stays tight despite minor kick‑drum distortion. The crystal‑clear soundboard capture makes this one of the best early‑66 recordings.
ai_show_review.review: The March 25, 1966 Trouper's Club gig captures the Grateful Dead in their raw Warlocks era, delivering a tightly knit R&B set that still feels fresh decades later. From the opening “Stealin'” through a brief jam and into Pigpen’s booming organ on “I’m A Hog For You Baby”, the band never loses its momentum – Jerry’s guitar is fiery (if occasionally a hair out of tune) and his vocals cut through with unmistakable passion. Bob Weir adds a surf‑guitar flash that complements the early‑66 vibe, while Phil’s bass anchors the groove even though it sits low in the mix. Pigpen’s organ dominates the soundstage, glorious and sometimes a touch loud, but it propels songs like “Hey Little One” and “You Don't Have To Ask” to standout status. Bill Kreutzmann keeps a solid pulse, with only a brief kick‑drum distortion on “Next Time You See Me”. The crystal‑clear soundboard source captures every nuance, making this recording one of the clearest snapshots of the Dead’s formative years.

best_recording.reason: Crystal‑clear early‑66 soundboard capture with excellent fidelity, prominent Pigpen organ and minimal tape noise.
